reason: The cited evidence (E3) supports the general concept that nonequilibrium processes can create unique SRO states, but no evidence is provided for the specific claims that laser modulation creates temperature plateaus for in-situ annealing, that such SRO can buffer thermal stresses, or that real-time monitoring can verify SRO formation. The processing window premise is unsupported by the cited evidence, which discusses different energy densities for other purposes.
premises: Laser power modulation can create transient temperature plateaus enabling in-situ annealing during LPBF.
In-situ annealing during LPBF can drive formation of a nonequilibrium short-range order (SRO) state.
A nonequilibrium SRO state can buffer thermal stresses and reduce defect formation.
Real-time temperature and spectroscopic monitoring can verify the development of the nonequilibrium SRO state.
Reduced volumetric energy density (100-150 J/mm³) with controlled dwells is suitable for processing AlCrFeNiSi.
